gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Victron Orion-Tr 48/12-20A isolated converter accepts 32–70 V input. That window covers a 48 V lead-acid cart, and it also covers a 48 V (51.2 V) lithium conversion whose included charger runs at 58.4 V, as on the Vatrer and Redodo kits. Its output is only 20 A continuous at a trimmable 10–15 V, so a powered soundbar plus cart lights needs a second unit in parallel (Victron says these can be paralleled) or a lighter load.
standout_why: Cited golfcartbase.com says only that 12 V gear needs a DC-DC reducer 'with enough continuous current'. It gives no input range, no amp figure and nothing on lithium. The cited mtx.com page returned 403 and I could not read it. Uncited cartvoltage.com (rank 3) already says to use a reducer with an input ceiling above 58.4 V and to size it at 30 A or more for a 200 W RMS soundbar with lights and horn. It names the Victron Orion-Tr but gives no input window and no output-current limit, and it does not tie 58.4 V to a named lithium kit's charger. A top result already has part of the finding, so the score is 1.
kit_items: 48→12 V converter: Victron Orion-Tr 48/12-20A isolated (ORI481224110). Its 32–70 V input covers 48 V lead-acid and lithium packs up to the 58.4 V charge voltage. Output trims from 10 to 15 V, which suits soundbars that shut down at high input voltage (cartvoltage.com reports this for an ECOXGEAR bar at about 14.2 V). It is rated 20 A continuous, so add a second unit in parallel if the soundbar and lights together need more than 20 A.

Powered 12 V soundbar: a 12 V DC bar fused at 10–15 A on its own positive lead, such as the ECOXGEAR SoundExtreme SE26. Its 15 A blade fuse and 12 VDC / 10 A input come from search results and retailer listings that I could not open, so they are not in findings.

Battery context, not part of the audio cart: if the cart has been converted to Vatrer or Redodo 48 V lithium, the included charger is 58.4 V, so the converter's input must go above 58.4 V. The Orion-Tr's 70 V maximum does.
